q2.note: Gives H2 with both parts of the deciding reason: database=h2 in application.properties and no datasource URL, so Spring Boot creates an embedded H2 from the runtime dependency.
q2.label: none

q3.reason_quote: `CacheConfiguration` creates the `vets` cache with `new MutableConfiguration<>().setStatisticsEnabled(true)`. JCache's default expiry for that is "eternal"
q3.note: Right lifetime, mixed reason: it states the JCache MutableConfiguration/eternal default as fact and only hedges the Caffeine cache manager fallback ('I expect'), which the marking rule scores as partial.
q3.label: none

q4.reason_quote: That method compares names with `equalsIgnoreCase` (`Owner.getPet(String, boolean)`), so it finds Max.
q4.note: Says no and gives both deciding mechanisms (controller's equalsIgnoreCase check and the case-insensitive unique constraint); the quoted message 'already exists' is wrong but counts only as an unsupported claim.
q4.label: none

q5.reason_quote: The match works because `owners.last_name` is `VARCHAR_IGNORECASE` in the H2 schema.
q5.note: Gives both Davises on the list page with the deciding reason (case-sensitive prefix query rescued by H2's VARCHAR_IGNORECASE column) and the Postgres contrast.
q5.label: none

q6.note: All six steps are present in order with the right classes and methods, Spring MVC is credited with invoking loadPetWithVisit before the handler, and the save is described as cascading from owner to pets to visits; no service layer or VisitRepository is invented.

1.quote: The form has `date` and `description` fields and posts back to the same URL.

2.quote: Next it runs the `@ModelAttribute` methods: `VisitController.loadPetWithVisit` calls `OwnerRepository.findById(ownerId)`.

3.quote: `VisitController.processNewVisitForm` rejects any date that isn't after today. If there are any errors, it shows the form again.

4.quote: `Owner.addVisit(petId, visit)` checks its arguments, finds the pet and calls `Pet.addVisit`. The visit is already in the pet's `Set`, so this changes nothing.

5.quote: The merge cascades from `Owner.pets` to `Pet.visits` (both `CascadeType.ALL`). When the transaction commits, Hibernate flushes and inserts a new row into `visits`

6.quote: The controller adds the flash message "Your visit has been booked" and redirects to `/owners/{ownerId}`.
